questions.q: The path was so __________ that we had to walk in single file.
questions.tip: 'Narrow' means not wide, and walking in single file only makes sense on a path too thin for two.

questions.q: My grandmother's hands were __________ from years of gardening.
questions.tip: Years of gardening make skin 'rough' — hard and uneven — so 'soft' is the opposite of what hard work does.

questions.q: The puppy was __________ and would not stop chewing my shoe.
questions.tip: 'Mischievous' means naughty in a playful way, fitting a puppy that keeps chewing shoes; 'obedient' is the opposite.

questions.q: We had to __________ our voices because the baby was asleep.
questions.tip: You 'lower' your voice to make it softer; 'raise' would wake the sleeping baby.

questions.q: The milk had turned __________ and smelt terrible.
questions.tip: Milk that has gone off turns 'sour' — sharp and unpleasant — which explains the terrible smell.

questions.q: He gave a __________ answer that told us almost nothing.
questions.tip: 'Vague' means unclear and lacking detail, matching an answer that told us almost nothing; 'detailed' says the opposite.

questions.q: The pavement was __________ after the rain, so I walked carefully.
questions.tip: 'Slippery' means so smooth and wet that feet slide, which is why you would walk carefully after rain.

questions.q: My little sister is very __________ and cries at loud noises.
questions.tip: 'Timid' means easily frightened, which explains crying at loud noises; 'brave' is its opposite.

questions.q: The old gate __________ loudly when we pushed it open.
questions.tip: An old gate 'creaked', making a harsh squeaking noise; whispering, humming and singing all belong to voices.

questions.q: She __________ the letter into four and put it in her pocket.
questions.tip: You 'folded' paper into four to make it small enough for a pocket; 'tore' would ruin the letter.

questions.q: The soup was __________, so I added more water.
questions.tip: 'Thick' soup is too heavy and needs water to thin it; you would not water down 'thin' soup.

questions.q: He was __________ after running all the way home.
questions.tip: 'Breathless' means out of breath, exactly what running all the way home does to you.

questions.q: The kitten __________ under the sofa when the doorbell rang.
questions.tip: 'Darted' means moved suddenly and very fast, fitting a kitten startled by the doorbell; 'strolled' is far too slow.

questions.q: My father is __________ about punctuality and hates being late.
questions.tip: Someone 'strict' insists that rules are kept, which explains hating lateness; 'relaxed' and 'careless' are opposites.

questions.q: The classroom was __________ with only three pupils inside.
questions.tip: With only three pupils inside, the room seemed 'empty'; 'crowded' and 'packed' mean the exact opposite.

questions.q: We __________ the rubbish into the correct bins.
questions.tip: 'Sorted' means separated into groups, which is what putting rubbish into the correct bins means; 'mixed' is opposite.

questions.q: The bread was __________ and difficult to chew.
questions.tip: 'Stale' bread is old, dry and hard, which is why it was difficult to chew; 'fresh' is opposite.

questions.q: She spoke __________ so that everyone at the back could hear.
questions.tip: 'Loudly' means with a strong voice, which people at the back need; 'quietly' and 'softly' are opposites.

questions.q: My uncle is __________ and tells jokes all through dinner.
questions.tip: 'Humorous' means funny and amusing, fitting someone who tells jokes all dinner; 'serious' and 'grumpy' are opposites.

questions.q: The room grew __________ as the sun went down.
questions.tip: 'Dimmer' means less bright, which is what happens to a room as the sun goes down.

questions.q: He __________ the heavy box across the floor.
questions.tip: You 'dragged' something heavy by pulling it along the floor, because it was too heavy to lift.

questions.q: The teacher was __________ with us for forgetting our books.
questions.tip: 'Annoyed' means slightly angry, the natural feeling about forgotten books; 'pleased' and 'grateful' do not suit a mistake.

questions.q: The water in the stream was perfectly __________.
questions.tip: 'Clear' water is completely see-through; 'muddy', 'dirty' and 'cloudy' all mean you cannot see through it.

questions.q: My brother is __________ and never shares his snacks.
questions.tip: 'Selfish' means thinking only of yourself, which explains never sharing snacks; 'generous' is its opposite.

questions.q: We __________ the tent before the rain started.
questions.tip: You 'pitch' a tent, meaning put it up — a fixed phrase; 'packed' and 'folded' mean putting it away.

questions.q: The floor was __________ after we mopped it.
questions.tip: 'Gleaming' means shining and spotlessly clean, which is how a floor looks after mopping; 'filthy' is opposite.

questions.q: He __________ the ball to me and I caught it.
questions.tip: 'Tossed' means threw lightly and gently, which fits a ball that was easily caught.

questions.q: The medicine tasted __________, but it made me feel better.
questions.tip: 'Bitter' is the sharp, unpleasant taste medicine often has; 'sweet' would not need the word 'but'.

questions.q: My cousin is __________ and can never sit still.
questions.tip: 'Restless' means unable to keep still, exactly what the sentence describes; 'calm' and 'sleepy' are opposites.

questions.q: The bag was __________ so the books fell out.
questions.tip: A 'torn' bag has a hole in it, so the books could fall out; 'sealed' would keep them in.

questions.q: She was __________ when she heard she had won.
questions.tip: 'Overjoyed' means extremely happy, the natural feeling on hearing that you have won.

questions.q: The road __________ sharply to the left.
questions.tip: A road that 'curved' bends round, and only this word fits 'sharply to the left'.

questions.q: The soup was __________ hot so I blew on it.
questions.tip: 'Scalding' means hot enough to burn, so you blow on it; 'barely' and 'slightly' are far too weak.

questions.q: He __________ the window to let in some fresh air.
questions.tip: You 'opened' a window to let air in; 'shut' and 'locked' would keep the fresh air out.

questions.q: The old photograph had become __________ over the years.
questions.tip: 'Faded' means the colour has slowly grown paler, which is what happens to old photographs.

questions.q: My grandfather walks with a __________ because of his bad knee.
questions.tip: A walking 'stick' supports someone with a bad knee; brooms and brushes are only for sweeping.

questions.q: The class was __________ when the principal walked in.
questions.tip: 'Silent' means completely without sound, the usual reaction when the principal enters; 'rowdy' is the opposite.

questions.q: She __________ the cake into eight equal pieces.
questions.tip: 'Divided' means separated into parts, which is what cutting a cake into eight equal pieces does.

questions.q: The kitten's fur was soft and __________.
questions.tip: 'Fluffy' means light and furry to touch, which goes naturally with soft fur; 'rough' contradicts 'soft'.

questions.q: We were __________ to find the shop already closed.
questions.tip: 'Disappointed' means sad because something you hoped for did not happen, such as finding the shop shut.

questions.q: The wind __________ the leaves across the field.
questions.tip: 'Scattered' means blew them apart in all directions; 'gathered' means the opposite, bringing them together.

questions.q: He is a __________ boy who always helps the younger pupils.
questions.tip: 'Thoughtful' means considerate towards others, which explains helping younger pupils; 'selfish' and 'rude' are opposites.

questions.q: The ice cream began to __________ in my hand.
questions.tip: 'Melt' means turn from solid into liquid, which a warm hand does to ice cream; 'freeze' is opposite.

questions.q: The hall was __________ with over three hundred people.
questions.tip: 'Packed' means completely full of people, which three hundred people would make a hall; 'empty' is opposite.

questions.q: She __________ at the joke until her sides hurt.
questions.tip: 'Chuckled' means laughed, the only laughing word here; 'wept', 'sighed' and 'frowned' all show unhappiness.

questions.q: The pencil was __________, so I could not write with it.
questions.tip: A 'blunt' pencil has no point left, so it cannot write; 'sharp' is its opposite.

questions.q: My mother was __________ that I had cleaned my room without being asked.
questions.tip: 'Pleased' means happy and satisfied, the natural feeling about a room cleaned without being asked.

questions.q: The dog __________ at the postman every morning.
questions.tip: Dogs 'bark'; purring belongs to cats, and humming or whistling to people.

questions.q: The path through the forest was __________ and hard to follow.
questions.tip: A 'winding' path twists and turns, which is why it is hard to follow; 'straight' is opposite.

questions.q: He was __________ after two nights of poor sleep.
questions.tip: 'Exhausted' means extremely tired, which two nights of poor sleep would cause; 'energetic' and 'alert' are opposites.

questions.q: The manager listened to the complaint with __________ patience.
questions.tip: 'Remarkable' means unusually great, so it praises the patience; 'noisy' and 'careless' cannot describe patience at all.

questions.q: Her handwriting was so __________ that the teacher asked her to copy it out again.
questions.tip: 'Untidy' means messy, which is why the teacher made her copy it again; 'neat' would need no rewriting.

questions.q: He made a __________ recovery and was back at training within a fortnight.
questions.tip: 'Swift' means very quick, matching a recovery completed within a fortnight; 'slow' contradicts that short time.

questions.q: The instructions were __________ and left nobody in any doubt.
questions.tip: 'Unambiguous' means having only one possible meaning, which is why nobody was left in any doubt.

questions.q: A __________ crowd had gathered outside the stadium long before the gates opened.
questions.tip: 'Sizeable' means fairly large, fitting a crowd gathered early; 'sparse' and 'tiny' would mean too few people.

questions.q: She was __________ about her chances and expected to lose.
questions.tip: 'Pessimistic' means expecting the worst, which matches expecting to lose; 'optimistic' and 'confident' are opposites.

questions.q: The old warehouse had been left to __________ for twenty years.
questions.tip: 'Decay' means to rot and slowly fall apart, which is what an abandoned building does.

questions.q: His excuse was so __________ that even the youngest pupil saw through it.
questions.tip: 'Feeble' means weak and unconvincing, so even young pupils saw through it; 'solid' and 'convincing' are opposites.

questions.q: The team's performance was __________; they won one match and lost the next.
questions.tip: 'Erratic' means changing unpredictably, matching winning one match then losing; 'consistent' and 'reliable' mean steady.

questions.q: The volunteers worked __________ through the night to clear the debris.
questions.tip: 'Tirelessly' means without stopping to rest, fitting work that lasted all night; 'briefly' and 'lazily' are opposites.

questions.q: She spoke with such __________ that nobody dared interrupt.
questions.tip: 'Authority' means confident command that makes people obey, so nobody dared interrupt; 'doubt' would invite interruption.

questions.q: Word of the cancellation spread __________ and by noon everyone knew.
questions.tip: 'Swiftly' means very quickly, which is how news must travel if everybody knows by noon.

questions.q: He was __________ to leave the party, as he was enjoying himself.
questions.tip: 'Reluctant' means unwilling, fitting someone still enjoying the party; 'eager' and 'keen' mean wanting to go.

questions.q: The evidence was so __________ that the case was dismissed.
questions.tip: 'Scanty' means far too little, and weak evidence is why a case is dismissed; 'conclusive' would prove it.

questions.q: Her __________ comment about his cooking upset him for days.
questions.tip: 'Thoughtless' means said without caring about feelings, which explains days of upset; 'polite' and 'kind' are opposites.

questions.q: The pianist's performance __________ the entire audience.
questions.tip: 'Enthralled' means held everyone spellbound with delight, the expected effect of a fine pianist.

questions.q: After the storm, the flood water slowly __________.
questions.tip: 'Receded' means moved back and went down, which floodwater does after a storm; 'rose' is the opposite.

questions.q: He accepted the award with genuine __________.
questions.tip: 'Humility' means being modest rather than boastful, which 'genuine' praises; 'arrogance' and 'conceit' are opposites.

questions.q: The two witnesses gave __________ accounts of the accident.
questions.tip: 'Conflicting' means disagreeing with each other, the reason for mentioning two witnesses; 'matching' and 'identical' mean the same.

questions.q: The soil in that corner is __________, so nothing grows there.
questions.tip: 'Barren' land is so poor that nothing can grow there; 'fertile' and 'rich' mean the opposite.

questions.q: She is __________ punctual and has never once been late.
questions.tip: 'Invariably' means always, without exception, matching never once being late; 'seldom' and 'rarely' mean hardly ever.

questions.q: The meal was __________ and left us all wanting more.
questions.tip: 'Meagre' means far too small an amount, which is why everyone still wanted more; 'filling' is opposite.

questions.q: His __________ for cycling kept him training through the monsoon.
questions.tip: 'Passion' means a very strong love for something, strong enough to keep you training through the monsoon.

questions.q: The librarian gave us a __________ look when we started laughing.
questions.tip: A 'stern' look is serious and disapproving, the look a librarian gives pupils who start laughing.

questions.q: The building was __________ damaged by the fire and had to be demolished.
questions.tip: 'Severely' means very badly, the only degree serious enough to force demolition; 'slightly' and 'barely' are too weak.

questions.q: She was praised for her __________ in rescuing the trapped kitten.
questions.tip: 'Bravery' means courage in danger, which earns praise for a rescue; 'cowardice' and 'panic' would not.

questions.q: The teacher __________ the class for their excellent behaviour.
questions.tip: 'Commended' means praised formally, which excellent behaviour deserves; 'scolded' and 'blamed' are for bad behaviour.

questions.q: His __________ knowledge of birds impressed the park ranger.
questions.tip: 'Extensive' means very wide and covering a great deal, which is why the ranger was impressed.

questions.q: The room fell __________ silent when the results were announced.
questions.tip: 'Utterly' means completely, the only word that strengthens 'silent'; 'almost' and 'nearly' would weaken it.

questions.q: The stray dog was so __________ that we could count its ribs.
questions.tip: 'Emaciated' means extremely thin from hunger, which is why the ribs showed; 'plump' is the opposite.

questions.q: He __________ the blame rather than let his friend be punished.
questions.tip: To 'shoulder' blame is to accept and carry it yourself, protecting his friend; 'shifted' means passing it on.

questions.q: The smell of the durian was __________ and filled the whole corridor.
questions.tip: 'Pungent' means having a very strong, sharp smell, which is why it filled the corridor; 'faint' is opposite.

questions.q: Their friendship __________ over many years of shared difficulty.
questions.tip: 'Deepened' means grew stronger, which shared hardship does to friendship; 'faded' and 'weakened' are opposites.

questions.q: The decision was __________; no appeal would be heard.
questions.tip: 'Irreversible' means impossible to change back, which is why no appeal was allowed; 'temporary' is the opposite.

questions.q: She dismissed the story as __________ nonsense.
questions.tip: Here 'utter' means complete or total, as in the set phrase 'utter nonsense'; 'credible' means believable.

questions.q: The road was __________ with potholes after months of rain.
questions.tip: 'Riddled' means full of holes all over, the usual word used with potholes; 'smooth' contradicts it.

questions.q: He made a __________ effort to tidy up, and it showed.
questions.tip: A 'token' effort is a tiny one made only for show, which is why it showed so plainly.

questions.q: The referee's decision provoked __________ from both sets of fans.
questions.tip: 'Fury' means violent anger, the feeling a bad decision 'provoked' in both sets of fans.

questions.q: My grandmother's advice proved __________ years later.
questions.tip: 'Invaluable' means extremely valuable, so the advice proved well worth having; 'worthless' and 'useless' are opposites.

questions.q: The kitten's __________ curiosity led it into the washing machine.
questions.tip: 'Insatiable' means impossible to satisfy, explaining curiosity strong enough to lead it into a washing machine.

questions.q: The hikers pressed on __________, despite the heat.
questions.tip: 'Doggedly' means stubbornly refusing to give up, which fits pressing on 'despite' the heat.

questions.q: His explanation was __________ enough to satisfy the strictest examiner.
questions.tip: 'Thorough' means complete and leaving nothing out, which even the strictest examiner would accept; 'vague' is opposite.

questions.q: He read the announcement in a __________ voice that put half the hall to sleep.
questions.tip: A 'toneless' voice is flat and without expression, which is why listeners fell asleep; 'lively' is opposite.

questions.q: She gave a __________ nod and walked on without stopping.
questions.tip: 'Curt' means so short it seems rude, matching walking on without stopping; 'warm' is the opposite.

questions.q: The old bridge was in a __________ state and closed to traffic.
questions.tip: 'Perilous' means dangerous, which is why the bridge was closed; 'sturdy', 'sound' and 'solid' mean safe.

questions.q: He is __________ about his diet and will not touch fried food.
questions.tip: 'Fastidious' means very fussy about details, fitting someone refusing all fried food; 'casual' and 'flexible' are opposites.

questions.q: The room was __________ furnished — a bed, a desk and nothing more.
questions.tip: 'Sparsely' means with very little, matching just a bed and a desk; 'lavishly' means the opposite.

questions.q: Towards the end of the long hike, our spirits began to __________.
questions.tip: Spirits that 'sag' sink and grow low, as tiredness causes late in a hike; 'soar' is opposite.

questions.q: The little boy clung to his mother, __________ of the strangers.
questions.tip: 'Wary' means cautious and distrustful, which explains clinging to his mother near strangers; 'fond' is the opposite.

questions.q: The award was a fitting __________ of forty years of service.
questions.tip: An 'acknowledgement' is public recognition of what someone has done, fitting an award for forty years' service.

questions.q: The witness's account was __________, changing three times in an hour.
questions.tip: 'Incoherent' means muddled and not making sense; an account changing three times cannot be 'consistent'.

questions.q: His __________ manner made the new pupils feel welcome at once.
questions.tip: 'Affable' means warm and easy to talk to, which is why the new pupils felt welcome.

questions.q: The scientist was __________ in her testing, repeating each experiment nine times.
questions.tip: 'Meticulous' means extremely careful about small details, matching repeating each experiment nine times.

questions.q: The proposal was met with __________ from every member of the committee.
questions.tip: 'Scepticism' means doubt; 'met with' usually introduces resistance, and the other three all mean the committee agreed.

questions.q: She is admired for her __________; she treats every pupil exactly alike.
questions.tip: 'Impartiality' means treating everyone equally and fairly, exactly what 'treats every pupil alike' describes.

questions.q: The politician gave an __________ reply that committed him to nothing.
questions.tip: 'Evasive' means dodging a straight answer, which is how a reply commits him to nothing.

questions.q: After the argument there was a __________ peace that nobody trusted.
questions.tip: A 'fragile' peace could break easily, which fits a peace nobody trusted; the others mean long-lasting.

questions.q: His account of the journey was so __________ that we felt we had been there.
questions.tip: 'Vivid' means so clear and lifelike that you can picture it, as though you were there.

questions.q: The old scholar was __________ and would talk for hours on any subject.
questions.tip: 'Garrulous' means very talkative; 'taciturn' is the trap, since it means saying very little.

questions.q: The rules were applied __________, with no exceptions for anyone.
questions.tip: 'Rigidly' means strictly and without bending, which matches 'no exceptions for anyone'.

questions.q: Her praise was so __________ that I suspected she did not mean it.
questions.tip: 'Effusive' means gushing and over-the-top, which is why the praise sounded insincere.

questions.q: The plan was __________ from the start and never had a chance.
questions.tip: 'Doomed' means certain to fail from the start, matching 'never had a chance'.

questions.q: He spoke with a __________ that came from thirty years of practice.
questions.tip: 'Fluency' means speaking smoothly and easily, the natural result of thirty years' practice.

questions.q: The two theories are __________; both cannot be correct.
questions.tip: 'Irreconcilable' means the two cannot both be made to fit; 'compatible' means the opposite.

questions.q: The village has remained largely __________ by tourism.
questions.tip: 'Remained' shows the village stayed as it was, so 'untouched' — unspoilt by tourism — fits.

questions.q: His __________ to detail is what makes his models so impressive.
questions.tip: 'Attention to detail' is a set phrase meaning careful notice of small things; the others mean ignoring it.

questions.q: The queue melted away __________ once the counter closed.
questions.tip: 'Abruptly' means suddenly and without warning, fitting a queue vanishing the moment the counter closed.

questions.q: She was __________ in her refusal and would not discuss it further.
questions.tip: 'Adamant' means completely firm and unwilling to change your mind, so she refused to discuss it.

questions.q: The report was criticised for being __________ and hard to verify.
questions.tip: 'Speculative' means based on guesswork rather than proof, which is why it was hard to verify.

questions.q: The coach's criticism was harsh but not __________ — every point was fair.
questions.tip: 'Unwarranted' means undeserved or unjustified, and 'every point was fair' shows the criticism was deserved.

questions.q: He has an __________ appetite for reading and finishes four books a month.
questions.tip: 'Insatiable' means impossible to satisfy, matching someone who devours four books every month.

questions.q: The mistake was __________ and cost the company a great deal.
questions.tip: 'Costly' means expensive, echoing 'cost the company a great deal'; the others all mean unimportant.

questions.q: Her explanation was so __________ that even the youngest pupils followed it.
questions.tip: 'Lucid' means clear and easy to follow; 'convoluted' is the trap, meaning twisted and confusing.

questions.q: The old man's memory was __________ and he recalled events from 1962.
questions.tip: 'Prodigious' means remarkably great, fitting a memory that still recalls events from 1962.

questions.q: They reached a __________ after four hours of negotiation.
questions.tip: 'Compromise' means an agreement in which each side gives way; 'deadlock' is the trap, meaning no agreement.

questions.q: Her fingers moved so __________ over the strings that we could barely follow them.
questions.tip: 'Nimbly' means quickly and lightly, which is why her fingers were hard to follow.

questions.q: His first attempt was __________, but by the fifth he was competent.
questions.tip: 'But' signals a contrast with 'competent', so the first attempt was 'dismal' — thoroughly poor.

questions.q: The driver was fined for __________ the speed limit.
questions.tip: 'Exceeding' means going beyond the limit, which is what earns a fine; 'observing' means obeying it.

questions.q: She accepted the setback with quiet __________.
questions.tip: 'Stoicism' means bearing trouble calmly without complaint, which matches the clue word 'quiet'.

questions.q: The path became __________ after the landslide and was closed.
questions.tip: 'Impassable' means impossible to travel along, which is why the path had to be closed.

questions.q: The teacher's tone was __________, and nobody argued.
questions.tip: 'Peremptory' means so commanding that argument is impossible, matching 'nobody argued'.

questions.q: His arguments were __________ and won over the whole hall.
questions.tip: 'Compelling' means so convincing that people are won over; 'flimsy' arguments would persuade nobody.

questions.q: The disease spread with alarming __________ through the district.
questions.tip: 'Rapidity' means great speed, and only speed could make the spread 'alarming'.

questions.q: He is __________ of criticism and takes every remark personally.
questions.tip: 'Intolerant of' means unable to put up with, which fits taking every remark personally.

questions.q: The museum houses an __________ collection of Ming porcelain.
questions.tip: 'Unrivalled' means having no equal, the kind of praise a fine museum collection earns.

questions.q: The decision was made after much __________ deliberation.
questions.tip: 'Deliberation' means weighing things up slowly, so it pairs with 'careful', never with 'hasty' or 'brief'.

questions.q: His reply was __________ and left the question unanswered.
questions.tip: 'Oblique' means indirect and roundabout, which is why the question was left unanswered.

questions.q: The volunteers' __________ during the flood was widely praised.
questions.tip: 'Fortitude' means brave endurance in hardship, the quality worth praising during a flood.

questions.q: The two brothers have __________ temperaments; one is calm, the other volatile.
questions.tip: 'Divergent' means clearly different and moving apart, matching one calm brother and one volatile one.

questions.q: She spoke of her childhood with obvious __________.
questions.tip: 'Affection' means warm fondness, the natural feeling behind speaking obviously happily of one's childhood.

questions.q: The plan was __________ complicated for a class of nine-year-olds.
questions.tip: 'Needlessly' means unnecessarily, showing the plan was more complicated than nine-year-olds required.

questions.q: His __________ was such that he returned every cent he had found.
questions.tip: 'Integrity' means firm honesty, which is why he returned every cent he had found.

questions.q: The evidence, though __________, was enough to convince the panel.
questions.tip: 'Though' signals weaker evidence, and 'circumstantial' means indirect — suggesting guilt without proving it outright.

questions.q: The old recipe has been handed down through __________ of the family.
questions.tip: 'Generations' are the successive parents and children of a family, the only group a recipe passes through.

questions.q: He gave a __________ account, leaving out nothing of importance.
questions.tip: 'Comprehensive' means complete and covering everything, which is why nothing important was left out.

questions.q: The announcement was greeted with __________ applause.
questions.tip: 'Rapturous' means wildly delighted — real applause, unlike 'silent' applause, which is a contradiction.

questions.q: Her curiosity about insects was __________ rather than passing.
questions.tip: 'Rather than passing' demands a word meaning long-lasting, and 'abiding' means exactly that.

questions.q: The two accounts, read side by side, were plainly __________.
questions.tip: 'Contradictory' means each account says the opposite of the other, so both cannot be true.

questions.q: He was __________ enough to admit that he had been wrong.
questions.tip: 'Candid' means frankly honest, and only honesty lets someone admit being wrong; pride would prevent it.

questions.q: The team's __________ in the final ten minutes won them the match.
questions.tip: 'Tenacity' means refusing to give up, which is how a team wins in the closing minutes.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **enormous**?
questions.tip: 'Enormous' means extremely large, so 'gigantic' matches; 'tiny' and 'narrow' describe small size or width instead.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **courageous**?
questions.tip: 'Courageous' means brave when facing danger, which is what 'valiant' means; 'timid' is the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **abandon**?
questions.tip: 'Abandon' means to leave something behind for good, and 'desert' here is the verb, not the sandy place.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **conceal**?
questions.tip: 'Conceal' means to keep something out of sight, while 'reveal' and 'display' mean the opposite, to show it.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **weary**?
questions.tip: 'Weary' means very tired; do not mix it up with 'wary', which means careful or cautious.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **peculiar**?
questions.tip: 'Peculiar' means strange or unusual, so 'ordinary', 'common' and 'plain' are its opposites.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **assist**?
questions.tip: 'Assist' means to help someone, while 'hinder' means almost the opposite, to get in their way.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **furious**?
questions.tip: 'Furious' means extremely angry, so 'calm' and 'content' are opposites rather than close matches.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **scarce**?
questions.tip: 'Scarce' means hard to find because there is very little; 'cheap' is about price, not amount.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **commence**?
questions.tip: 'Commence' is a formal word meaning to begin, so 'finish' and 'cancel' are not close in meaning.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **fragile**?
questions.tip: 'Fragile' means easily broken, so 'delicate' fits; 'sturdy' and 'tough' mean strong instead.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **abundant**?
questions.tip: 'Abundant' means there is more than enough of something, so 'scarce' and 'empty' are opposites.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **reluctant**?
questions.tip: 'Reluctant' means unwilling to do something, so 'eager', 'keen' and 'ready' are all opposites.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **vanish**?
questions.tip: 'Vanish' means to disappear suddenly, while 'appear' means to come into sight, the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **stubborn**?
questions.tip: 'Stubborn' means refusing to change your mind, which is exactly what 'obstinate' means.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **precise**?
questions.tip: 'Precise' means exact and accurate, so 'vague' and 'rough' mean the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **mend**?
questions.tip: 'Mend' means to fix something that is damaged, so 'break' is its opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **halt**?
questions.tip: 'Halt' means to stop moving or stop happening, so 'continue' and 'begin' are opposites.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **gloomy**?
questions.tip: 'Gloomy' means dark and miserable, which is what 'dismal' means; 'cheerful' is the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **swift**?
questions.tip: 'Swift' means very fast; 'steady' only means even or regular in speed, which is not the same.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **generous**?
questions.tip: 'Generous' means happy to give and share, and 'liberal' here means giving freely, nothing political.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **anxious**?
questions.tip: 'Anxious' means worried about what might happen, which is what 'apprehensive' means.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **enquire**?
questions.tip: 'Enquire' means to ask for information, so 'answer' and 'reply' are the opposite action.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **sufficient**?
questions.tip: 'Sufficient' means just enough, while 'excessive' means far too much, which is not the same.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **detest**?
questions.tip: 'Detest' means to hate something strongly, so 'adore' and 'admire' are its opposites.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **wealthy**?
questions.tip: 'Wealthy' means having plenty of money, which is what 'affluent' means; 'needy' is the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **attempt**?
questions.tip: 'Attempt' means to try to do something, and 'endeavour' is a more formal word for trying.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **vacant**?
questions.tip: 'Vacant' means empty and not in use, so 'occupied' is its opposite even though it sounds related.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **tremble**?
questions.tip: 'Tremble' means to shake slightly from cold or fear, while 'freeze' means to stay completely still.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **conclude**?
questions.tip: 'Conclude' means to bring something to an end, while 'pause' is only a short break.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **cautious**?
questions.tip: 'Cautious' means taking care to avoid danger, so 'reckless', 'bold' and 'hasty' are opposites.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **brief**?
questions.tip: 'Brief' means short, and 'concise' means saying a lot in few words; 'lengthy' is the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **permit**?
questions.tip: 'Permit' means to allow something, so 'forbid' and 'prevent' mean the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **strenuous**?
questions.tip: 'Strenuous' means needing a great deal of effort, so 'easy' and 'effortless' are opposites.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **grateful**?
questions.tip: 'Grateful' means thankful for something; 'ungrateful' looks almost the same but means the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **obtain**?
questions.tip: 'Obtain' means to get or gain something, which is what 'acquire' means; 'lose' is the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **feeble**?
questions.tip: 'Feeble' means weak and lacking strength, so 'robust', 'sturdy' and 'powerful' are opposites.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **hostile**?
questions.tip: 'Hostile' means unfriendly and ready to fight, so 'friendly', 'warm' and 'kind' are opposites.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **swiftly**?
questions.tip: 'Swiftly' means quickly, so 'hastily' fits best; 'gradually' means slowly, bit by bit.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to **remarkable**?
questions.tip: 'Remarkable' means so unusual that people notice it, so 'ordinary', 'common' and 'dull' are opposites.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **ancient**?
questions.tip: 'Ancient' means from very long ago, so 'antique', 'aged' and 'old' are synonyms, not opposites.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **permanent**?
questions.tip: 'Permanent' means lasting for ever, so its opposite is 'temporary', meaning only for a short time.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **humble**?
questions.tip: 'Humble' means not proud or boastful, so 'modest' and 'meek' are synonyms; 'arrogant' is the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **transparent**?
questions.tip: 'Transparent' means you can see right through it, while 'opaque' means light cannot pass through.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **increase**?
questions.tip: 'Increase' means to become larger, so 'diminish', meaning to become smaller, is its opposite.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **voluntary**?
questions.tip: 'Voluntary' means done by choice, so 'optional' and 'willing' are synonyms; 'compulsory' means you must.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **praise**?
questions.tip: 'Praise' means to say how good someone is, so 'applaud' and 'commend' are synonyms, not opposites.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **artificial**?
questions.tip: 'Artificial' means made by people rather than found in nature, so 'synthetic' and 'fake' are synonyms.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **accept**?
questions.tip: 'Accept' means to agree to take something, so 'receive' and 'welcome' are close, not opposite.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **shallow**?
questions.tip: 'Shallow' means not deep, so 'deep' is the opposite; 'flat' and 'level' describe a surface instead.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **generous**?
questions.tip: 'Generous' means happy to give and share, so 'miserly', meaning unwilling to spend, is its opposite.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **ascend**?
questions.tip: 'Ascend' means to go up, so 'climb', 'rise' and 'mount' are synonyms; 'descend' means to go down.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **guilty**?
questions.tip: 'Guilty' means having done wrong, while 'accused' and 'charged' only mean someone has been blamed.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **fertile**?
questions.tip: 'Fertile' land grows plenty, so 'productive' and 'lush' are synonyms; 'barren' land grows nothing.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **conceal**?
questions.tip: 'Conceal' means to keep out of sight, so 'hide', 'bury' and 'mask' are synonyms, not opposites.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **rigid**?
questions.tip: 'Rigid' means stiff and unable to bend, so 'hard', 'stiff' and 'firm' are synonyms instead.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **majority**?
questions.tip: 'Majority' means more than half, so 'bulk' and 'most' are synonyms; 'minority' is the smaller part.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **expand**?
questions.tip: 'Expand' means to grow bigger, so 'contract' here means to shrink, not a written agreement.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **optimistic**?
questions.tip: 'Optimistic' means expecting good things, so 'hopeful' and 'positive' are synonyms, not opposites.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **abundant**?
questions.tip: 'Abundant' means there is plenty, so 'ample' and 'plentiful' are synonyms; 'scarce' means very little.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **arrive**?
questions.tip: 'Arrive' means to reach a place, so 'depart' means to leave; 'approach' only means coming nearer.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **victory**?
questions.tip: 'Victory' means winning, so 'triumph' and 'success' are synonyms; 'defeat' means losing.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **tighten**?
questions.tip: 'Tighten' means to make something firmer, so 'fasten' and 'secure' are synonyms, not opposites.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **familiar**?
questions.tip: 'Familiar' means well known to you, so 'strange', meaning unknown or unusual, is its opposite.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **encourage**?
questions.tip: 'Encourage' means to give someone confidence to carry on, while 'discourage' takes that confidence away.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **wealthy**?
questions.tip: 'Wealthy' means rich, so 'affluent' and 'prosperous' are synonyms; 'impoverished' means made very poor.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **noisy**?
questions.tip: 'Noisy' means full of loud sound, so 'deafening' and 'rowdy' are synonyms; 'tranquil' means peaceful.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **construct**?
questions.tip: 'Construct' means to build, so 'erect' and 'assemble' are synonyms; 'demolish' means to knock down.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **ally**?
questions.tip: 'Ally' means someone who is on your side, so 'partner' and 'supporter' are synonyms, not opposites.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **obedient**?
questions.tip: 'Obedient' means doing as you are told, so 'dutiful' and 'docile' are synonyms; 'defiant' refuses.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **frequent**?
questions.tip: 'Frequent' means happening often, so 'rare' is the opposite; 'regular' just means at fixed times.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **retreat**?
questions.tip: 'Retreat' means to move back away from danger, so 'withdraw' and 'flee' are synonyms, not opposites.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **fatigue**?
questions.tip: 'Fatigue' means great tiredness, so 'vigour', meaning strength and energy, is its opposite.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **approximate**?
questions.tip: 'Approximate' means roughly right but not exact, so 'rough' and 'estimated' are synonyms instead.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **superior**?
questions.tip: 'Superior' means better or higher in rank, so 'inferior', meaning lower or worse, is its opposite.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **transparent** (of a person's motives)?
questions.tip: Here 'transparent' means open and easy to see through, so 'honest' and 'open' are synonyms.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **surplus**?
questions.tip: 'Surplus' means more than is needed, so 'excess' and 'spare' are synonyms; 'shortage' means too little.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **considerate**?
questions.tip: 'Considerate' means thoughtful of other people's feelings, and adding 'in-' flips it to the opposite.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **permit**?
questions.tip: 'Permit' means to allow, so 'let' and 'approve' are synonyms; 'prohibit' means to forbid.

questions.q: Which word is **opposite** in meaning to **fiction**?
questions.tip: 'Fiction' means made-up writing, so 'novel' and 'tale' are kinds of fiction; 'fact' is what is true.

questions.q: decide → The committee reached a __________ after two hours.
questions.tip: The noun is 'decision'.

questions.q: succeed → Her __________ surprised nobody who knew how hard she worked.
questions.tip: The subject slot needs a noun, so the verb 'succeed' becomes 'success'; 'successful' is an adjective.

questions.q: strong → We must __________ the fence before the storm.
questions.tip: Adjective becomes a verb with -en.

questions.q: beauty → The garden was truly __________.
questions.tip: After 'was' the slot describes the garden, so the noun 'beauty' becomes the adjective 'beautiful'.

questions.q: safe → Please read the __________ instructions first.
questions.tip: 'Safety' is the noun used before 'instructions' in this fixed pairing; 'safe instructions' would mean the instructions are safe.

questions.q: advise → She gave me some excellent __________.
questions.tip: The noun ends in -ce.

questions.q: know → His __________ of insects is remarkable.
questions.tip: The slot after 'His' needs a noun, so the verb 'know' becomes the noun 'knowledge'.

questions.q: high → They plan to __________ the wall by one metre.
questions.tip: 'Plan to' signals a verb, and '-en' turns the adjective 'high' into the verb 'heighten'.

questions.q: anger → The crowd grew __________ as the delay continued.
questions.tip: After 'grew' the slot describes the crowd, so the noun 'anger' becomes the adjective 'angry'.

questions.q: explain → His __________ was clear and convincing.
questions.tip: Note the spelling — no 'i'.

questions.q: proud → She spoke with obvious __________ about her daughter.
questions.tip: After 'with obvious' a noun is needed, and 'proud' has the irregular noun form 'pride'.

questions.q: apply → Please submit your __________ by Friday.
questions.tip: 'Your' signals a noun, so 'apply' becomes 'application'; 'appliance' means a machine, not a form.

questions.q: wide → They are going to __________ the road next year.
questions.tip: 'Going to' needs a verb, and '-en' turns 'wide' into 'widen', meaning to make wider.

questions.q: generous → His __________ towards the charity was well known.
questions.tip: 'His' before the blank signals a noun, so the adjective 'generous' becomes 'generosity'.

questions.q: discover → The __________ of the tomb made headlines.
questions.tip: 'The' and 'of' need a noun between them, so the verb 'discover' becomes 'discovery'.

questions.q: true → Nobody doubted the __________ of her story.
questions.tip: After 'the' a noun is needed, and 'true' has the irregular noun form 'truth'.

questions.q: able → His __________ to stay calm impressed everyone.
questions.tip: 'His' before the blank signals a noun, so the adjective 'able' becomes 'ability'.

questions.q: choose → You have made an excellent __________.
questions.tip: 'An excellent' signals a countable noun, so the verb 'choose' becomes the noun 'choice'.

questions.q: deep → Workers came to __________ the drain.
questions.tip: 'To' marks a verb, and '-en' turns 'deep' into 'deepen', meaning to make deeper.

questions.q: responsible → Taking care of the rabbit is my __________.
questions.tip: After 'my' a noun is needed, so the adjective 'responsible' becomes 'responsibility'.

questions.q: argue → They had a long __________ about the rules.
questions.tip: Drop the 'e' from 'argue'.

questions.q: happy → The children shouted with __________.
questions.tip: 'With' is a preposition and needs a noun, so 'happy' becomes 'happiness', with '-y' changing to '-i'.

questions.q: pronounce → Her __________ of French is excellent.
questions.tip: Note: no 'o' in the middle — pronunciation, not pronounciation.

questions.q: long → The interval was __________ by ten minutes.
questions.tip: The passive 'was ______ by' needs a past-tense verb, and 'long' gives 'lengthened'; 'longed' means yearned for.

questions.q: patient → She waited with great __________.
questions.tip: 'With great' signals a noun, so 'patient' becomes 'patience'; 'patients' would mean sick people.

questions.q: compete → There were forty entries in the __________.
questions.tip: 'The' before the blank needs a noun, so the verb 'compete' becomes 'competition'.

questions.q: dangerous → The __________ of the crossing is obvious to everyone.
questions.tip: 'The' and 'of' need a noun, so the adjective 'dangerous' becomes the noun 'danger'.

questions.q: describe → Her __________ of the scene was vivid.
questions.tip: Note the spelling — 'scription', not 'scribtion'.

questions.q: free → The prisoners were finally given their __________.
questions.tip: 'Their' signals a noun, and '-dom' turns the adjective 'free' into 'freedom'.

questions.q: perform → The __________ lasted two hours.
questions.tip: 'The' before the blank needs a noun, so 'perform' becomes 'performance'; 'performer' is a person.

questions.q: wise → We admired the __________ of her decision.
questions.tip: 'The' and 'of' need a noun, so the adjective 'wise' becomes the irregular noun 'wisdom'.

questions.q: inform → Thank you for the __________.
questions.tip: Uncountable — never 'informations'.

questions.q: poor → __________ is still a serious problem in some regions.
questions.tip: The subject of the sentence must be a noun, so the adjective 'poor' becomes 'poverty'.

questions.q: repeat → The __________ of the same mistake worried the coach.
questions.tip: Note: repetition, not 'repeatition'.

questions.q: anxious → Her __________ showed in her trembling hands.
questions.tip: 'Her' before the blank signals a noun, so the adjective 'anxious' becomes 'anxiety'.

questions.q: strength → Regular exercise will __________ your legs.
questions.tip: 'Will' needs a verb, and '-en' turns the noun 'strength' into the verb 'strengthen'.

questions.q: appear → His sudden __________ startled us all.
questions.tip: 'His sudden' signals a noun, so the verb 'appear' becomes 'appearance'.

questions.q: jealous → His __________ of his brother spoilt the celebration.
questions.tip: 'His' and 'of' need a noun between them, so the adjective 'jealous' becomes 'jealousy'.

questions.q: prove → There is no __________ that he took it.
questions.tip: 'No' before the blank signals a noun, so the verb 'prove' becomes the noun 'proof'.

questions.q: curious → Her __________ about the locked room grew daily.
questions.tip: 'Her' and 'about' need a noun between them, so the adjective 'curious' becomes 'curiosity'.

questions.q: simple → Let me __________ the instructions for you.
questions.tip: 'Let me' is followed by a verb, and '-ify' turns the adjective 'simple' into 'simplify'.

questions.q: warm → The crowd gave the team a __________ welcome. (warm)
questions.tip: Some words serve as both adjective and verb — no change is needed here.

questions.q: decide → He is a very __________ leader.
questions.tip: The adjective is 'decisive'.

questions.q: care → She is a __________ driver and has never had an accident.
questions.tip: The slot describes 'driver', so an adjective is needed; 'careless' would contradict never having an accident.

questions.q: help → Standing there complaining is completely __________.
questions.tip: The meaning is negative, so 'help' takes '-ful' and 'un-' to make the adjective 'unhelpful'.

questions.q: hope → After three failures he felt __________.
questions.tip: -less means 'without'.

questions.q: thought → It was a very __________ gift.
questions.tip: The slot describes 'gift', so the noun 'thought' takes '-ful' to make the adjective 'thoughtful'.

questions.q: attend → __________ at the talk was disappointing.
questions.tip: The subject slot needs a noun, so the verb 'attend' becomes 'attendance'; 'attendant' is a person.

questions.q: organise → The __________ of the event took six months.
questions.tip: 'The' and 'of' need a noun, so 'organise' becomes 'organisation', spelt with '-s-' in British English.

questions.q: persevere → Her __________ finally paid off.
questions.tip: Note the spelling — -ance, not -ence.

questions.q: After months of tension, the two departments finally __________.
questions.tip: 'Bury the hatchet' means to make peace after a quarrel, like putting a weapon away so it cannot be used.

questions.q: He announced the winner before the votes were counted — he really __________.
questions.tip: 'Jump the gun' means to start or act too soon, like a runner who moves before the starting gun fires.

questions.q: By not applying earlier, she __________ on the scholarship.
questions.tip: 'Miss the boat' means to lose a chance by being too late, like arriving after the boat has sailed.

questions.q: The youngest dancer __________ at the concert.
questions.tip: 'Steal the show' means to win all the attention and praise, even when others were expected to.

questions.q: That substitute goal completely __________ of the match.
questions.tip: 'Turn the tide' means to change a situation completely, usually from losing to winning.

questions.q: After the argument, a long talk finally __________.
questions.tip: 'Clear the air' means to talk openly so bad feelings disappear, like fresh air blowing away smoke.

questions.q: He was late, and to __________ he had forgotten the tickets.
questions.tip: 'Add insult to injury' means to make a bad situation even worse by doing something else unpleasant.

questions.q: Nobody wanted to __________ by questioning the teacher's decision.
questions.tip: 'Rock the boat' means to upset a calm situation by causing trouble or disagreeing.

questions.q: I was put in charge of the project and completely __________.
questions.tip: 'Drop the ball' means to be careless and fail at something you were trusted to do.

questions.q: Revising the night before an exam is __________.
questions.tip: 'Cutting it fine' means leaving yourself barely enough time, with almost no room for delay.

questions.q: Once we had passed the difficult section, the rest was __________.
questions.tip: 'Plain sailing' means easy and smooth, with no problems, like a ship on calm water.

questions.q: With a twenty-point lead, the match was __________.
questions.tip: 'In the bag' means already certain to be won or achieved.

questions.q: Whether the trip will go ahead is still __________.
questions.tip: 'Up in the air' means still undecided, like something floating that has not yet landed.

questions.q: After being caught twice, he is __________ with the discipline master.
questions.tip: 'On thin ice' means in a risky position where one more mistake brings trouble, like ice about to crack.

questions.q: The timetable is not __________ and may still change.
questions.tip: 'Set in stone' means fixed and impossible to change, like words carved into stone.

questions.q: He tried to __________ by blaming his younger brother.
questions.tip: 'Pass the buck' means to blame someone else or push your own responsibility onto them.

questions.q: Could you __________ while I go to the office?
questions.tip: 'Hold the fort' means to look after things while the person in charge is away.

questions.q: When the captain was injured, the vice-captain __________.
questions.tip: 'Take the reins' means to take charge, like a rider taking the reins to control a horse.

questions.q: His confession __________ on the whole mystery.
questions.tip: 'Shed light' means to make something clearer or easier to understand by giving new information.

questions.q: The teacher __________ on our plan by pointing out the cost.
questions.tip: 'Throw cold water' on an idea means to discourage it by pointing out the problems.

questions.q: I tried to remember her name but __________.
options: hit the nail on the head
questions.tip: 'Draw a blank' means to fail completely to remember or find something.

questions.q: Studying with Nadia was __________ — she explained everything clearly.
questions.tip: 'A breath of fresh air' means someone or something pleasantly new, easy and refreshing.

questions.q: Criticism is __________ to him; he never takes it personally.
questions.tip: "Water off a duck's back" means criticism with no effect, because water runs straight off oily duck feathers.

questions.q: Losing to a weaker team was __________ to swallow.
questions.tip: 'A bitter pill' means an unpleasant fact you must accept, like nasty-tasting medicine you must swallow.

questions.q: The news that the test was postponed was __________.
questions.tip: 'Music to our ears' means news that is very welcome and pleasant to hear.

questions.q: That leaking tap has been __________ for months.
questions.tip: 'A thorn in my side' means a constant annoyance that keeps bothering you, like a thorn you cannot remove.

questions.q: He passed the examination __________ — one mark above the pass mark.
options: by the skin of his teeth
questions.tip: 'By the skin of his teeth' means only just managing, succeeding by the narrowest possible margin.

questions.q: She passed __________, scoring the highest mark in the level.
options: by the skin of her teeth
on a wing and a prayer
questions.tip: 'With flying colours' means very successfully; ships once came home with their flags, or colours, still flying.

questions.q: Our team won __________; the score was 6–0.
questions.tip: 'Hands down' means winning easily and by a wide margin, with no real contest.

questions.q: He took the extra responsibility __________ and never complained.
options: by the skin of his teeth
questions.tip: 'Take it in his stride' means to handle something calmly, like a horse clearing a fence without breaking step.

questions.q: When the teacher asked who broke it, everyone __________.
options: let the cat out of the bag
questions.tip: 'Quiet as a mouse' means completely silent, saying nothing at all.

questions.q: Learning the piano at forty is difficult, but it is never __________.
questions.tip: 'Never too late' means you can still start or change something, whatever your age.

questions.q: Our old quarrel is __________ now; we are good friends.
questions.tip: 'Water under the bridge' means an unpleasant thing in the past that no longer matters, having flowed away.

questions.q: Trying to persuade him is __________ — he never changes his mind.
questions.tip: 'A lost cause' means something with no hope of succeeding, so the effort is wasted.

questions.q: She kept practising and eventually __________.
questions.tip: 'Struck gold' means found great success or something very valuable, like a miner finding gold.

questions.q: After six failed attempts he __________.
questions.tip: 'Throw in the towel' means to give up; a boxer's helpers threw a towel in to stop the fight.

questions.q: Do not __________ — wait until the results are confirmed.
questions.tip: 'Count your chickens' means to assume success too early, from 'do not count your chickens before they hatch'.

questions.q: __________ — the bus does not leave for another hour.
questions.tip: 'Hold your horses' means wait and slow down, as a driver pulls back horses to halt them.

questions.q: He explained it so clearly that the penny finally __________.
questions.tip: 'The penny dropped' means you suddenly understood, like a coin dropping to make an old slot machine work.

questions.q: Finding a good second-hand bicycle at that price was a real __________.
questions.tip: 'A steal' means something bought so cheaply that the bargain feels almost like stealing.

questions.q: The meeting was __________ because the chairman was ill.
questions.tip: 'Called off' means cancelled, so the meeting did not take place at all.

questions.q: She __________ the offer of help, saying she could manage alone.
questions.tip: 'Turn down' means to refuse or reject something that is offered to you.

questions.q: Please __________ your name and address on the form.
questions.tip: 'Fill in' means to write the details needed in the spaces on a form.

questions.q: He __________ smoking after his doctor's warning.
questions.tip: 'Give up' means to stop doing something for good, especially a habit.

questions.q: The thieves __________ with two paintings.
questions.tip: 'Make off' means to hurry away, usually after stealing something.

questions.q: I cannot __________ what this word says; the ink has smudged.
questions.tip: 'Make out' means to manage to see or read something that is unclear.

questions.q: They __________ the meeting until Thursday.
questions.tip: 'Put off' means to delay something until a later time.

questions.q: The fire brigade quickly __________ the blaze.
questions.tip: 'Put out' means to stop something burning, so the fire is extinguished.

questions.q: My cousins __________ us for three nights during the holidays.
questions.tip: 'Put up' someone means to give them a bed in your home for a night or more.

questions.q: We __________ an old friend at the airport.
questions.tip: 'Run into' means to meet someone by chance, without any plan to do so.

questions.q: The photocopier has __________ paper again.
questions.tip: 'Run out of' means to use up all of something, so none is left.

questions.q: Could you __________ these figures once more?
questions.tip: 'Go over' means to check or examine something carefully again.

questions.q: The milk has __________; do not drink it.
questions.tip: 'Gone off' means food or drink has spoilt and is no longer fit to eat.

questions.q: The alarm __________ at half past five.
questions.tip: 'Went off' means the alarm suddenly rang or sounded.

questions.q: She __________ her grandmother, both in looks and temper.
questions.tip: 'Take after' means to resemble an older relative in looks or in character.

questions.q: He has __________ far too much work this term.
questions.tip: 'Take on' means to accept extra work or responsibility, agreeing to do it.

questions.q: The plane __________ twenty minutes late.
questions.tip: 'Took off' means the plane left the ground and began flying.

questions.q: I could not __________ everything the guide said.
questions.tip: 'Take in' means to understand and absorb information you hear or read.

questions.q: His business really __________ after the article appeared.
questions.tip: 'Took off' here means grew very quickly and became successful.

questions.q: Please __________ the cat while we are away.
questions.tip: 'Look after' means to care for someone or something, keeping them safe and fed.

questions.q: The committee promised to __________ the complaint.
questions.tip: 'Look into' means to investigate a matter to find out the facts.

questions.q: I have always __________ my older sister.
questions.tip: 'Look up to' means to admire and respect someone.

questions.q: __________! There is a car coming.
questions.tip: 'Look out' means be careful, because there is danger.

questions.q: They __________ the old cinema to build flats.
questions.tip: 'Pull down' means to demolish a building, knocking it to the ground.

questions.q: Against all expectations, she __________ a remarkable victory.
questions.tip: 'Pull off' means to succeed in something difficult, often when nobody expected it.

questions.q: The car __________ outside our gate.
questions.tip: 'Pull up' means a vehicle slows down and comes to a stop.

questions.q: He __________ the family business when his father retired.
questions.tip: 'Take over' means to take control of something from whoever ran it before.

questions.q: The two sisters do not __________ at all.
questions.tip: 'Get along' means to have a friendly relationship with someone.

questions.q: It took him a year to __________ the disappointment.
questions.tip: 'Get over' means to recover from something upsetting and feel better again.

questions.q: We can __________ on very little during the holidays.
questions.tip: 'Get by' means to manage with only a little money or help.

questions.q: I could not __________ to the clinic; the line was busy.
questions.tip: 'Get through' means to succeed in reaching someone by telephone.

questions.q: He __________ the meeting because of a clash.
questions.tip: 'Back out of' means to withdraw from something you had agreed to do.

questions.q: Faced with the evidence, she finally __________.
questions.tip: 'Back down' means to stop arguing and admit you were wrong.

questions.q: Remember to __________ your work before you switch off.
questions.tip: 'Back up' means to save a second copy of your work in case it is lost.

questions.q: The conversation __________ when the teacher entered.
questions.tip: 'Break off' means to stop talking suddenly, before you have finished.

questions.q: A fire __________ in the storeroom overnight.
questions.tip: 'Break out' means a fire, war or disease starts suddenly.

questions.q: Thieves __________ through the kitchen window.
questions.tip: 'Break in' means to enter a building by force, usually in order to steal.

questions.q: He __________ in tears when he heard the news.
questions.tip: 'Broke down' means lost control of his feelings and began crying.

questions.q: Please __________ these leaflets to everyone in the hall.
questions.tip: 'Hand out' means to give one to each person in a group.

questions.q: The recipe has been __________ through four generations.
questions.tip: 'Handed down' means passed on from parents to children over several generations.

questions.q: A __________ of bees settled on the branch.
A __________ of wolves followed the deer.
A __________ of lions rested under the tree.
A __________ of fish swam past the reef.
A __________ of geese flew overhead.
A __________ of cattle grazed in the field.
A __________ of ants carried the crumb away.
A __________ of monkeys swung through the trees.
A __________ of kittens was found behind the shed.
A __________ of ships sailed into the harbour.
A __________ of thieves was arrested.
A __________ of musicians played at the wedding.
A __________ of sailors worked on deck.
A __________ of stars glittered above.
A __________ of grapes lay on the plate.
A __________ of flowers was delivered to the ward.
A __________ of books lined the shelf.
A __________ of keys jangled in his pocket.
A __________ of players trained every evening.
A __________ of sheep blocked the road.
Give me a __________ of advice before I decide.
questions.tip: 'Advice' is uncountable.

questions.q: She bought a __________ of bread at the bakery.
He ate three __________ of toast for breakfast.
There was not a single __________ of rice left in the bowl.
Please buy a __________ of soap.
We moved one __________ of furniture at a time.
questions.tip: 'Furniture' is uncountable.

questions.q: He checked in two __________ of luggage.
Add a __________ of salt to the soup.
She drank a __________ of water after the race.
There was a thick __________ of dust on the shelf.
